title: Applied ML weekly research scrapbook — quant & onboarding notes (wk of Aug 10–16, 2026)
content:
Purpose:
Quick, informal dump of research notes from the week — captures standup snippets, short experiment logs, blockers, and next steps related to quantization experiments, eval runs, and onboarding a new model variant. Not polished; meant for the team to pick up.

Hosts / attendees:
- Priya (lead)
- Miguel
- Sofia
- Liam
- Ad-hoc: platform-engineering (Sam), infra (Jess) for capacity checks

High-level summary (one-paragraph):
This week focused on two threads: (1) getting a new Llama2-13B-rlhf-derived variant through our onboarding checklist and initial benchmark suite, and (2) exploratory quant experiments to reduce serving memory/CU costs while monitoring downstream eval regressions. Early wins: 4-bit NF4 (GPTQ) reduced peak GPU memory by ~18–22% on our 2k-seqlen workload; latency impact negligible with current batching. Risk: on a narrow math QA set, exact-match fell by ~2.6% when aggressive per-channel scale clipping (clip=0.9) was applied — need to understand which layers are most sensitive.

Standup highlights / decisions:
- Decided to pause auto-rollout of quantized model to canary due to the math QA regression. (Decision: manual canary only after layer-sensitivity mitigation.)
- Action: Miguel to capture per-layer activation distributions and produce a delta heatmap for the top-12 layers (due Mon 2026-08-17).
- Blocker: V100 pool has conflicting reserved jobs Aug 18–19; Jess to request temporary burst to A100-48 for larger quant retrains.

Experiment log (concise):
1) Baseline onboarding eval: llama2-13b-rlhf-variant (untouched FP16)
- eval suite: 5k prompts sampled from product QA logs + math-short, code-snippet, and summary tasks
- metrics: avg latency 98ms/token (p50), mem 9.8GB (per-replica), EM(math) 42.3%, rouge-L( summarization ) 0.51
- notes: baseline stable; used for regression comparisons.

2) GPTQ 4-bit NF4 (per-tensor vs per-channel tries)
- config A: per-tensor NF4 (fastest encode path). result: mem 7.8GB (-20%), latency +3ms/token, EM(math) 40.1% (-2.2)
- config B: per-channel PF32 scale + NF4 weights (more accurate). result: mem 7.9GB (-19.5%), EM(math) 40.8% (-1.5)
- config C: per-channel + clip at 0.9 (aggressive). result: mem 7.6GB (-22.4%), EM(math) 39.7% (-2.6) — triggered the canary pause.
- profiler: top-K matmuls dominated time; quant decode overhead small.

3) INT8 symmetric (dynamic range) experiments
- run: int8-dyn, per-channel ouput scales for linear layers only (leave attention QKV as FP16)
- result: mem 8.4GB (-14%), EM(math) 41.7% (-0.6) — promising tradeoff
- notes: attention QKV sensitivity is high; recommend leave-attention-fp param in pipeline.

4) KV-cache effects + batching
- observation: quantized weights + aggressive batching increased transient host memory due to larger input queueing; need to tune batch timeouts.
- experiment: reduced max-batch-size by 12% and set batch-wait-ms=4 improved p99 tail by ~1.8% on QC tests.

Quick profiling outputs (snippets):
- sample command: ./bench/serve_profile --model ./models/llama2-13b-q4nf4 --seq 2048 --batch 8
- peak_gpu_mem: 7832MB
- p50_token_ms: 101
- p99_token_ms: 178

Open questions / hypotheses to validate:
- Which specific layers (embedding / early feed-forward / late attention) cause the largest EM drop when clipping scales? (Hypothesis: last 4 FFN layers are most sensitive.)
- Can we gain back EM by hybridizing: keep top-k layers FP16 and quantize rest to q4? (Plan: run k=4,6,8 hybrid tests.)
- Are eval regressions concentrated on math problems with large constants or chained reasoning? Need per-example diffs.

Action items (who / what / when):
- Miguel: generate per-layer activation delta heatmap + sensitivity ranking. DUE: 2026-08-17.
- Sofia: run hybrid quant tests (k=4,6,8 FP16 top layers) on 2k prompt subset and produce summary. DUE: 2026-08-19.
- Liam: add targeted unit tests in eval harness for math-chain examples where the model failed after quant. DUE: 2026-08-18.
- Priya: update onboarding checklist with an explicit "layer-sensitivity" gate and document canary rules. DUE: 2026-08-20.
- Sam (platform): provision A100-48 for retrain/quant tasks Aug 18–20 (requested).

Notes on onboarding steps completed for the new variant:
- Model registered in model-registry (PR #198).
- Security scan: key material OK, LFS artifacts verified (Sofia).
- Small-scale smoke tests passed: sample generation, tokenization sanity, replayed 50 prod prompts.
- Pending: performance profile for multi-region routing (need dedicated capacity window).

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: rolling quantized model without layered sensitivity checks could cause user-visible regressions. Mitigation: hold auto-rollout; require EM/regression thresholds on critical eval subsets before canary.
- Risk: dataset licensing for 3rd-party math test set unclear. Mitigation: stop-gap use internal synthetic set while legal clarifies.

Mini-retro (what worked / didn't):
- Worked: quick iteration cadence on small quant configs (can iterate overnight). Team was responsive to perf surprises.
- Didn't work: insufficient per-example diffs in the eval harness — slowed root-cause of math regression. Need more granular diff tools.

Raw notes / fragment ideas to capture later:
- Try "scale-preserving rounding" (experiment idea from Miguel) for narrow distribution heads.
- Explore whether the tokenizer offset differences cause mismatched evaluation on exact-match; small whitespace tokenization differences can flip EM. Add canonicalized whitespace preproc.
- Consider "selective fine-tune after quant" on a small dataset to recover EM for fragile tasks (cheap 1–2 epoch light-tune on 10k examples).

Next week's focus:
- Complete hybrid quant runs, layer sensitivity ranking, and per-example diffs. If hybrid k=6 shows <0.5% EM delta, prepare manual canary steps.
- Platform: secure A100 burst and schedule longer eval runs (10k prompts) for final decision.

If you pick this up: start with Miguel's heatmap and Sofia's hybrid results. The content above should give you immediate pointers for which steps to run next.

-- Priya
